engine.streaming: speak-easy sentence pipeline (SherpaTextToSpeech.speak, depth 1): segment waveforms, not incremental within a segment; full mode is one generateAsync call
engine.chunkPolicy: planSegments: first chunk is the first clause or 4 words of sentence 1, then whole sentences; trimSilence trims each chunk and appends a 150 ms gap
engine.cancellation: between segments (the host returns the generator); a depth 1 lookahead synth already started runs to completion

loadDetail.note: loadMs is TtsSynth.create (digest verify, native load, frontend) plus session open

Here is where things stand on the release. The migration ran overnight and finished without errors, so the new tables are live in staging. I checked the dashboards this morning, and response times are back under two hundred milliseconds. Two small issues remain. The export button still times out on very large projects, and one of the email templates shows the old logo. I have opened tickets for both and assigned them to Maya, who expects to close them by Thursday. If you are happy with that plan, I will schedule the production rollout for Friday morning, before the team meeting. Let me know if you would rather wait until next week, and I will move everything back.

I finished reading the three papers you flagged last night. The first one claims a forty percent speed up, but only on short prompts, and their test machine had twice our memory. The second paper is more useful: it shows that splitting text at commas cuts the wait before speech by about half. The third is mostly a survey, so I only kept the summary table. Overall, I think the comma trick is worth trying first, because it needs no new model and could ship in a day. I wrote up the details in the research folder, with links to each paper and the numbers I checked. Tell me if you want a shorter version for the team update on Monday.
